title: Authentication
detail: Six unique Security 4625 records crossed a five event, same account, five minute threshold.
limit: One nonexistent synthetic account; no successful login.

raw.threshold: 5 events per target account within 5 minutes

rule.description: Five Windows failed logons for the same account within five minutes: CyberLab_Ph3_NoUser

origin: KALI-ATTACK preflight to WIN-LAB-01; authentication evidence remained endpoint local
kaliRole: Authentication surface preflight only. No authentication attempt was sent.
method: Six failed secondary-logon attempts targeted `CyberLab_Ph3_NoUser`. The account does not exist and the credential string was synthetic and redacted from evidence.
observables: Synthetic target `CyberLab_Ph3_NoUser`; Windows event 4625; Wazuh rules 60122 and 100201; six unique record IDs.
investigation: Confirmed a single target account, six unique event records, a five-second observed window, no successful authentication, and no real identity impact.
containment: Stopped the test after six failures. The synthetic account did not exist, so no account disablement was required.
remediation: Use MFA, account lockout or smart throttling, stale-credential hygiene, and alert enrichment with source and success/failure context.
retest: PASS: six unique 4625 events generated one custom rule 100201 alert at the configured threshold.

title: Encoded PowerShell
proof: One command. A complete evidence chain.
detail: A benign encoded command appeared in PowerShell 4104 and Wazuh 92057, then in a documented VYOMRIX investigation.
limit: Benign marker only; no download or network action.

rule.description: Powershell.exe spawned a powershell process which executed a base64 encoded command

kaliRole: Not applicable for endpoint local execution.
method: A child PowerShell process decoded and ran only `Write-Output 'CyberLab-Phase3-Encoded-Benign'`.
observables: `powershell.exe`, `-EncodedCommand`, parent process, benign decoded marker, Wazuh alert ID.
investigation: Decoded the command, reviewed parent/child context, confirmed the user and timestamp, and verified no network action.
containment: The process exited normally and made no network connection. No endpoint protection was disabled.
remediation: Constrain PowerShell where appropriate, retain script-block logging, use signed administrative scripts, and investigate encoded content in context.
retest: PASS: new 4104 and Wazuh 92057 evidence matched the existing Sigma selection.

title: Scheduled task
detail: Security 4698 and Wazuh 60228 recorded the visible task registration; the task was removed.
limit: Task payload execution was not observed.

raw.scenario: harmless scheduled task creation and execution

kaliRole: Not applicable for endpoint local task creation.
method: Registered a one-time task with a benign file-writing action, requested execution, then removed it. The payload file was not produced before cleanup, so execution is not claimed.
observables: Task `CyberLab-Phase3-Benign`; Security 4698; Wazuh rule 60228; task XML in sanitized alert evidence.
investigation: Reviewed task name, task content, creator, timestamp, intended action, and post-test absence of the task.
containment: Unregistered the task and verified it no longer exists. No stealth or startup trigger was used.
remediation: Restrict task creation, audit task registration, monitor unusual actions and user-writable paths, and inventory approved task baselines.
retest: PASS for creation detection and cleanup. Payload execution was not observed and remains explicitly outside the claim.

title: Credential access simulation
proof: The denied request is the finding.
detail: Windows denied a query only LSASS handle request. Wazuh recorded discovery; Sysmon Event 10 was absent.
limit: No credential read, memory dump, or Event 10. LSASS Sigma NOT_TRIGGERED.

raw.scenario: credential-access behavioural simulation using process query only
raw.conclusion: Credential-access behaviour was emulated. No real credentials were harvested.

windows.scriptBlockText: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' $start = Get-Date Add-Type -TypeDefinition @' using System; using System.Runtime.InteropServices; public static class Phase3ProcessQuery {   [DllImport(\"kernel32.dll\", SetLastError=true)] public static extern IntPtr OpenProcess(uint access, bool inherit, int pid);   [DllImport(\"kernel32.dll\")] public static extern bool CloseHandle(IntPtr handle); } '@ $lsass = Get-Process -Name lsass $queryLimitedInformation = 0x1000 $handle = [Phase3ProcessQuery]::OpenProcess($queryLimitedInformation, $false, $lsass.Id) $opened = $handle -ne [IntPtr]::Zero if ($opened) { [Phase3ProcessQuery]::CloseHandle($handle) | Out-Null } Start-Sleep -Seconds 3 $events = foreach ($event in Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational'; Id=10; StartTime=$start } -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {   [xml]$xml = $event.ToXml(); $fields = @{}   foreach ($item in $xml.Event.EventData.Data) { $fields[$item.Name] = [string]$item.'#text' }   if ($fields.TargetImage -like '*\\lsass.exe' -and $fields.SourceImage -like '*\\powershell.exe') {     [ordered]@{ event_id=10; record_id=$event.RecordId; timestamp_utc=$event.TimeCreated.ToUniversalTime().ToStrin

kaliRole: Not applicable for the denied local query.
method: Requested only `PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION (0x1000)` against LSASS and immediately closed any handle. Windows denied the request.
observables: PowerShell process discovery; target `lsass.exe`; requested access 0x1000; handle-open result false; Event 10 count zero.
investigation: Confirmed the handle was not opened, no memory-read API was used, no artifact containing credentials existed, and no Event 10 was emitted.
containment: No handle opened and no credential material existed. The one-shot process ended immediately.
remediation: Protect LSASS, enable Credential Guard where compatible, retain Event 10 telemetry, and baseline approved security products.
retest: PARTIAL: safe access was denied and no Event 10 resulted. Riskier tooling was deliberately not used.

title: Host only web findings
detail: KALI-ATTACK sent controlled requests to an isolated purpose built app that recorded SQL injection bypass and traversal constrained to synthetic lab files.
limit: No Wazuh alert. The service was stopped and its request log was preserved.
method:
## Verified evidence flow

```text
KALI-ATTACK 192.168.56.10
to controlled HTTP requests
to synthetic application 192.168.56.1:8085
to application request records
to authored AppSec Sigma selections
to VYOMRIX INC-7890B5F0
to analyst containment and retest
```

Kali was the genuine request source. The application bound only to the host only adapter.
observables:
| Source | Record | Result |
|---|---|---|
| KALI-ATTACK | Sanitized curl transcript | Source 192.168.56.10 confirmed |
| Synthetic application | requests.jsonl | SQL injection bypass and path traversal confirmed |
| WAZUH-MGR | Primary behavior alert | Not observed |
| VYOMRIX | INC-7890B5F0 | Kali timeline and evidence references added |
investigation: The application log identifies 192.168.56.10 as the request source. The SQL injection request returned the synthetic admin row. The traversal request returned only `SYNTHETIC-LAB-DATA-NOT-A-REAL-SECRET`. The normal login retest returned unauthenticated. This establishes Kali as the real request source without claiming access to a public target or real data.
containment: The temporary service was stopped. Port 8085 no longer listened on 192.168.56.1. The request log remained readable and its SHA256 remained c1a113a1618f6e3927fb280edae83c24ec294a49b0a2977ef0eb16c412fc8973.
remediation: Use parameterized queries; resolve and enforce an allowlisted content root; return generic errors; add structured security logging and tests.
retest: The normal synthetic credentials remained unauthenticated. The service was then stopped and port 8085 was confirmed closed. A remediated application was not deployed, so code remediation requires further validation.

title: Synthetic data transfer
detail: WIN-LAB-01 transferred three synthetic files to the isolated Kali collector. Source staging and received payloads were removed.
detection: Archive staging Sigma / built in Wazuh 91819 context
limit: No Internet egress, command and control, or real data. Wazuh 91819 is supporting endpoint context, not a direct transfer detector.
method:
## Verified evidence flow

```text
WIN-LAB-01 192.168.56.20
to synthetic archive creation
to HTTP transfer inside 192.168.56.0/24
to KALI-ATTACK collector 192.168.56.10:8090
to PowerShell 4104 and Wazuh 91819
to VYOMRIX INC-4C4C2C05
to receiver shutdown and payload removal
```

Kali was the genuine isolated collection endpoint. The transfer never left the host only network.
observables:
| Source | Record | Result |
|---|---|---|
| WIN-LAB-01 | windows-transfer.json | HTTP 201, 489 bytes, source cleanup confirmed |
| KALI-ATTACK | kali-collector.json | Source 192.168.56.20 and destination 192.168.56.10:8090 confirmed |
| PowerShell | Event 4104 record 3406 | Archive and transfer script preserved |
| WAZUH-MGR | Rule 91819 | Alert 1789381207.5448611 observed |
| VYOMRIX | INC-4C4C2C05 | Kali collector and Wazuh evidence references added |

Source and collector SHA256: 69755c314f43aef1f88ec80e2ec6f3e3fb78fcac8b1b15dc4ff7812b7478b936.
investigation: WIN-LAB-01 created three clearly synthetic files and compressed them into a 489 byte archive. KALI-ATTACK received the archive at 192.168.56.10:8090. Both systems calculated SHA256 69755c314f43aef1f88ec80e2ec6f3e3fb78fcac8b1b15dc4ff7812b7478b936. PowerShell 4104 record 3406 and Wazuh alert 1789381207.5448611 provide endpoint context. The collector record proves network receipt.
containment: Windows staging was removed. The Kali receiver process was stopped. Port 8090 was confirmed closed. The received synthetic archive and temporary receiver files were deleted after hash verification.
remediation: Apply data classification, DLP, destination allowlists, proxy logging, archive monitoring, and least-privilege controls.
retest: The corrected transfer returned HTTP 201. Source and collector hashes matched. Windows cleanup completed. Kali port 8090 closed after containment. No default route or non host only adapter was present.
